name: Alpinarium Galtür
kurzbeschreibung: The Alpinarium Galtür combines a monumental avalanche protection wall with a modern experience museum exploring the high-alpine habitat.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Alpinarium Galtür in the rear Paznaun valley is a globally unique documentation centre and experience museum: it is integrated directly into Galtür's massive avalanche protection wall, which measures 345 metres in length and up to 19 metres in height. This striking structure was erected as a direct architectural and societal response to the devastating avalanche disaster of 23 February 1999, in which 31 people lost their lives. At an altitude of 1,584 metres above sea level, the museum combines contemporary memorial culture with a fascinating interactive exhibition on the alpine habitat, the culture of the Walser settlers, and the relationship between humanity and the high-alpine environment.

History & Architecture

Following the 1999 avalanche catastrophe, the municipality of Galtür decided to build a monumental protective barrier to shield the village from future avalanches descending from the steep flanks of the Sonnberg and Grisköpfe peaks. The Tyrolean architectural firm Falch conceived the protective wall not as an austere concrete barrier, but harmoniously integrated the museum building into the rear wall structure. The exterior facade was clad with more than 20,000 tonnes of regional natural stone and nestles against the valley like a modern fortress. Officially opened in 2003, the Alpinarium has received multiple international awards, including a nomination for the prestigious European Museum of the Year Award and the Austrian Museum Quality Seal. At its core is the permanent exhibition "GANZ OBEN", which brings to life the formation of avalanches, historical survival in alpine valleys, and the pioneering feats of alpinism through multimedia room installations, eyewitness accounts, and scientific interactive stations.

Visiting & Getting There

The Alpinarium is open during both the summer and winter seasons (early June to mid-October as well as mid-December until after Easter, Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 18:00, closed on Mondays). Regular admission prices (as of 2025/2026): adults €10.00, seniors and students €8.50, children aged 6 to 15 €5.50, children under 6 free. Holders of the Silvretta Card Premium guest card enjoy free or discounted admission. By car, Galtür can be reached via the Inntal autobahn A12 or Arlberg expressway S16 to the Pians exit, and from there via the B188 (Paznauntalstraße) through Ischgl to Galtür. Parking spaces are available directly at the building. By public transport, travel by train (ÖBB/Railjet) to Landeck-Zams station and transfer to VVT bus line 260, which runs regularly to the Galtür Dorfplatz stop (approx. 5 minutes walk to the Alpinarium).

Tips

The entire museum building is barrier-free and equipped with wheelchair-accessible elevators, wide passageways, and accessible restrooms. In addition to the exhibition spaces, the building houses an indoor bouldering wall of around 70 m² in the café "Gefrorene Wasser", which opens up spectacular views of the three-thousand-metre peaks of the Silvretta through floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows. Plan around 1.5 to 2 hours for your visit.
